'''''Pentzia''''' is a genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Anthemideae|chamomile tribe]] within the [[Asteraceae|sunflower family]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/3586552#page/68/mode/1up Thunberg, Carl Peter. 1800. Prodromus plantarum Capensium :quas in promontorio Bonæ Spei Africes, annis 1772-1775 page 145] in Latin</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40004183 Tropicos, ''Pentzia'' Thunb.]</ref> Species are native to southern Africa, Chad, northwestern Africa, Somalia, and the southern Arabian Peninsula.<ref name = powo/> One species ''(P. incana)'' is naturalized in Australia and in the southwestern United States.<ref name=y>{{cite book |series=[[Flora of North America]] |title=Asteraceae |volume=19–21 |chapter=''Pentzia'' Thunberg, Prodr. Pl. Cap. 145. 1800 |author=David J. Keil |page=543 |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=124465 |isbn=978-0-19-530563-0}}</ref>

The genus is named for Swedish plant collector Hendrik Christian Pentz (1738–1803).<ref name=y/>

===Formerly included===
Several species once considered part of ''Pentzia'' now regarded as better suited to other genera, including ''[[Foveolina]] [[Gymnopentzia]] [[Inulanthera]] [[Myxopappus]] [[Oncosiphon]]'', and ''[[Phymaspermum]]''.<ref name=x>[http://dixon.iplantcollaborative.org/compositaeweb/Default.aspx?Page=AdvNameSearch Flann, C (ed) 2009+ Global Compositae Checklist ] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20141106174748/http://dixon.iplantcollaborative.org/CompositaeWeb/Default.aspx?Page=AdvNameSearch |date=2014-11-06}}</ref>
